dialog.body: Public Works storm line, this is Denise. City Hall's closed for the day, but I've got the line open. How can I help?

Oh, good, somebody's there. Hello, Denise. This is Carmela Grasso. I know it's almost seven at night and you're closed, that's why I'm calling the storm number. I figured it was the only one that'd pick up.
You figured right. What's going on, Mrs. Grasso?
It's the water. Three days after that nor'easter, Friday into Saturday, and it's still sitting there. Across the crosswalk by the bus stop, where the school kids wait. It's a pond, I'm telling you.
Still pooled three days later. Okay. Where is this exactly?

I'm at 191 Bellevue Avenue, and the crosswalk is right out front of me, down by where the old, what do you call it, the old trolley stop used to be. No, that's not right, that was years ago. The bus stop. Just the bus stop.
Got it, 191 Bellevue Avenue, crosswalk at the bus stop. Is the water covering the whole crosswalk?

Wall to wall, nearly. The kids can't stand on the curb because it's wet, so they're stepping out into the road to get around it. This morning I watched a little one in yellow boots go right out past the white line, and a car was coming. I almost went out there in my slippers.
That's not good with the cars coming through. Is it a storm drain that's clogged, do you think, or is it just low there?

Well, the drain is right there on the corner, and I can't see it. It's all leaves and sand and I don't know what. And the sidewalk, Denise, it's a sheet of mud and grit. You can't walk on it without sliding. I've lived here forty years and it never sat like this. Every time it rains it's the same, and nobody comes.
I hear you. I'm sorry, that's a mess. Have you called about this drain before, or is this the first time you've reported it?
I haven't called, no. I kept thinking somebody'd come with a truck after the storm. You see them sometimes. But nobody did, and it's Tuesday already.

Okay. Right now, after a storm like that, the crews are working through a long list of drains and cleanup. I'll put this in as a priority because of the kids and the road. Who you'd want checking it is our Public Works crew, and that's what this report does. I'll send it to them tonight.
So I don't call anybody else? That's what I was asking. Who do I call to get it checked?

You've called the right place. I'm entering it now as a clogged drain with standing water at a school crosswalk. If it gets worse or somebody's in danger, call the main emergency number. Otherwise, the crew will take it from here.

Well, I hope so. Because I'm sitting here in my pajamas, and it was two in the afternoon when I first looked out and saw it, and I've been in them ever since. I didn't want to go out and slip in that muck.
No, don't go out there in it. Stay put. Let me get the details right. Is the water deep enough that a car would splash through it?

Oh, the cars splash it. They go right through and spray the sidewalk. That's partly why it's mud, it keeps getting thrown up. It's a few inches at the deepest, by the curb. Like a big puddle, but it doesn't drain. It just sits.
Few inches by the curb, doesn't drain, debris on the grate. That's what I have. Which side of the street is the bus stop on, yours or across?
My side. The ocean side. No, wait, I always get that backwards. The side with my house. The odd numbers.
Odd-numbered side, in front of 191. Perfect. Do you want a call back when the crew's been out?
I would, yes. They can call me. It's 401-555-0183.
401-555-0183, I have that. Somebody may call you or just stop by the site. Either way it's logged under your name.
And how long, do you think? Just roughly. Because the kids are there at seven-thirty every morning.

I'd hope sometime tomorrow, since it's flagged for the school stop. If it's more backed up than it looks, they might have to come back with the bigger equipment. But tomorrow morning is the target I'm putting on it.
Tomorrow morning. All right. I'll be at the window, believe me. I'll be watching.
If you see them, that's your answer. And if nobody's there by midday, call this line back and mention the report from tonight.
I will. I'm not shy about it. It's been three days, Denise. Three days of those kids stepping into traffic.
Understood, and I'm glad you called. It's in the system now. Anything else you can see out there, like other drains that look blocked?
Not on my stretch. Down toward the corner it looks okay, it's just this one. The one that's right at the crosswalk.
Great, just the one. You take care, Mrs. Grasso, and stay warm in those pajamas.
Ha, I will. Thank you, dear. Goodnight.
Goodnight.
